entities.summary:
Canada is a country in North America, spanning ten provinces and three territories from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean and northward into the Arctic Ocean. The second-largest country by total area (9,984,670 km²), it shares the world's longest international border with the United States. With a population of 38 million, Canada is one of the world's most sparsely populated large nations, with 90% of its people concentrated within 200 km of the US border.

Indigenous peoples inhabited the Canadian territory for at least 14,000 years before European contact. French (1534) and British (1497) exploration and colonization established the colonial rivalry that shaped Canadian identity. The British Conquest of New France (1763) created the tension between Francophone Quebec and Anglophone Canada that remains central to Canadian politics. Confederation in 1867 established the Dominion of Canada as a self-governing British domain; full sovereignty came with the Statute of Westminster (1931) and the Constitution Act (1982).

Canada developed as a resource economy — furs, fish, wheat, timber, and eventually oil sands — while building one of the world's most comprehensive welfare states in the 20th century. Universal healthcare (Medicare, 1966), multiculturalism as official policy (1971), and the Charter of Rights and Freedoms (1982) define Canadian civic identity. Canada-US relations — dominated by the largest bilateral trade relationship in history — and reconciliation with First Nations peoples are the defining political challenges of the 21st century.
